image_description: A side-profile view of a sorrel horse standing in a grassy field with trees in the background. The horse has a reddish-brown coat, a flaxen (lighter) mane and tail, and a white blaze on its face. It appears to be wearing a halter.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated head with large expressive eyes and mobile ears.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible in profile, showing an elongated shape typical of equines. The eye is visible and appears normal; ears are upright.
The neck connects smoothly to the shoulder and head, showing appropriate musculature and arch for a horse.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Athletic build with tall, lean proportions at the withers.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The horse displays a standard athletic equine build with visible withers and a level topline.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Uniform brownish-orange to light chestnut coat coloration with no black points.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coat is a consistent reddish-brown (chestnut/sorrel). There are no black points (mane, tail, or lower legs are not black).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Mane and tail same color as body or lighter (flaxen).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mane and tail are visibly lighter than the body coat, consistent with a flaxen chestnut/sorrel phenotype.
The chest depth and back line appear structurally sound and proportional to the rest of the body.
The tail is visible hanging down, appearing long and hairy, consistent with equine anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Long slender legs with single hoof per foot.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: All four legs are visible. They are slender and end in single hooves. No extra limbs or structural deformities are observed.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific breed/color classification (Sorrel/Chestnut) and rule out misclassification as other equines or mammals.
To verify the skeletal structure and limb connectivity, ensuring no subtle fusion or missing joints in the legs.
To check for edge bleeding between the horse's coat/mane and the background foliage, a common AI artifact.
To assess overall image sharpness, texture consistency of the fur/grass, and detect any low-level generative noise.

focus_areas: Mane and tail texture vs. background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the hooves; AI often blurs them into the grass. Verify that the 'white blaze' on the face is a distinct marking and not a texture glitch. Ensure the halter straps (if present) follow logical geometry around the head.
